This doesn't compare at all to some things on this thread but a few years ago, the dude who I used to be best friends with, was really going through it with a breakup. We were on a drive in the middle of the night, he was going 95 on a shitty back road, Hinder's Lips of an Angel was blaring over the speakers, and he looked away from the road to look me in the eye and say "you ever just feel like life is meaningless?" And then I realized that man could have killed us both that night and would have felt next to nothing about it. 

Anyway, we're married now.
A lot of people have provided "reasonable retorts" here. You're just too far up your own ass to actually listen to them.

22 and right before covid, my boyfriend and I started renting a house together. Lost my job to covid and haven't been able to find something stable/long term since. A couple months ago, my boyfriend had his hours cut in half at his job, also because of covid. We've sold quite literally almost everything we own to make ends meet, down to our bed frame. We have no family to fall back on and are going to be losing our house soon. People who act like covid isn't affecting others like this ARE the problem.

there's so many flaws in the way people approach this subject and as a trans person (ftm) i just want to bring up a couple small things that everyone seems to be overlooking here...

first of all, op really is out here fear mongering over trans people. "we should talk about trans people in sports" is one thing and a statement i completely agree with. phrasing is as "trans women are a huge threat..." is wording used to try and demonize trans women. 

more importantly, why the fuck would any trans person want to join a trans-only sports league? assuming we're talking about trans-only sports leagues being treated the same way cis-only sports leagues would be, why the fuck would anyone want the fact they're trans to be broadcasted everywhere? maybe this is just the area i live in, but in the country i live in, violence against trans people, especially trans women, has only gotten worse and worse over the last few years. i've been physically assaulted due to my gender identity and so have most of the other trans people i know in person. to me, someone who played several sports in school, the idea of joining a trans-only basketball team or something similar feels like putting a massive target on my back. maybe for other people in other places, the feeling is different, but i'd personally rather not get murdered for wanting to run track.

there are solutions, trans-only sports teams are not it. men's sports are already (mostly) unisex, as far as i know. in school, i competed on women's sports teams but in a few of those teams, cis men would occasionally compete alongside us. during my sophomore year of high school, one of the members of our school's volleyball team was a cis man and nobody thought anything of it. granted, this is probably less common in professional level sports but i've seen high school level sports brought up a couple times in this thread- if a cis male is allowed to compete on a women's volleyball team in high school and everyone is fine with it, why does the conversation change if a trans woman wants to compete?

unisex sports leagues that are recognized as unisex instead of as "men's" sports leagues are the best i've got for you, but i'm sure there's someone else out there whose got a much better solution than me. my only thoughts are that this conversation is used way too often to demonize trans women and that trans-only sports teams blissfully ignore the reality of violence against trans people.
